questions.q: What is the difference between a default instance and a named instance during Setup's Instance Configuration screen?
options: There is no difference — the terms are interchangeable
A default instance requires SQL Server Browser; a named instance does not
A default instance is unnamed, one per machine; a named instance has its own name and multiple can coexist on one machine
A named instance can only be installed on Linux, never Windows
questions.explain: Named instances require SQL Server Browser running so clients can resolve the dynamic port; a machine can have one default instance plus any number of named instances.

questions.q: What must you set during the Database Engine Configuration screen if you choose Mixed Mode authentication?
options: The server's IP address
Nothing extra — Mixed Mode requires no additional configuration
The Windows domain administrator's password
The sa password, right there in the wizard
questions.explain: Mixed Mode allows both Windows logins and SQL Server logins like sa, and the wizard requires you to set the sa password when you choose it.

questions.q: Why does the Data Directories screen matter, per this lesson?
options: It has no real effect since paths can be freely changed after install with no downside
It only appears when installing Analysis Services
It's where the file-layout decision from planning actually gets applied, setting default paths for data, log, and tempdb files
It only affects where log files for the setup process itself are written
questions.explain: This screen is exactly why the file-layout decision needed to happen during planning, before this moment in the wizard.

questions.q: Which of the following does the Setup wizard NOT configure, according to this lesson?
options: Feature selection
Default data and log file paths
Max server memory and MAXDOP
Authentication mode
questions.explain: Max server memory, MAXDOP, cost threshold for parallelism, tempdb file count, and backup compression default are all post-install configuration steps, not part of Setup.

questions.q: Why is Windows Authentication mode described as more secure than Mixed Mode when every client can authenticate via Active Directory?
options: It trusts only Windows/AD logins, eliminating the need for a separate SQL Server login like sa with its own password to manage
It is only available in Enterprise edition
It automatically encrypts all data at rest
It disables all network connectivity to the instance
questions.explain: Windows-only mode removes SQL Server logins (including sa) from the picture entirely when AD authentication already covers every client.
